objects: a graph with node feature vectors from a countable space; at each layer, the multiset of a node's neighbor feature vectors
assumptions: node input features come from a countable universe
multisets of neighbor features are of bounded size
guarantees: formal theorem: any GNN is at most as powerful as the Weisfeiler-Lehman isomorphism test
formal theorem: sum aggregation is injective over bounded multisets, matching WL's power exactly
formal proof: mean aggregation only captures proportions, not exact counts
formal proof: max aggregation only captures presence, ignoring counts entirely
empirical: state-of-the-art or comparable accuracy on 9 graph classification benchmarks
formalism.operation: sum the multiset of neighbor feature vectors, combine with the node's own previous feature, pass through an MLP
